chapter_title_en: Star-Swap Art: Shao Yanong’s Final Gambit
chapter_seo_title: Star-Swap Art in Desolate Era: Shao Yanong’s Treacherous Entry into Wu Jiang Hall
chapter_meta_description: Shao Yanong drops the humble act and uses a priceless Star-Swap Disk to bypass the foreign Dao-soldiers and enter the final sub-palace. But inside Wu Jiang Hall, his true ambitions surface.
og_title: Star-Swap Art: How Shao Yanong Cheated the Foreign Army
og_description: A single-use spatial treasure swaps a whole party past 20,000 Dao-soldiers—but Shao Yanong’s mind is already on treasures and beautiful women.
twitter_title: The Mask Falls: Shao Yanong’s Cold Triumph in Wu Jiang Hall
twitter_description: With his Star-Swap Disk, Shao Yanong outmaneuvers an army. But inside the main hall, he starts eyeing his allies’ treasures.

lore_anchors.definition: A spatial divine ability that swaps the positions of two targets over a short distance. Shao Yanong’s version is a single-use consumable disc, evidence of the Shao clan’s immense wealth.
The main sub-palace of Celestial Immortal Wu Jiang’s estate, named after the immortal himself. It is expected to hold the estate’s central nexus.
A high noble rank within the Grand Xia Dynasty. Shao Yanong is vying for this position, and this estate acquisition is part of the clan’s test.
Magical armor sets that allow multiple soldiers to merge their power into a giant, sentient phantom. The foreign race’s Wave and Yaksha Dao-soldiers are examples of this formation type.
One of Shao Yanong’s most powerful treasures (already used and lost earlier in the arc), its exact function not yet fully revealed but implied to be a powerful binding or sealing tool.
